transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-08
Start time: 16:17 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Tom Baxter (Redwood CSM), Jasmine Patel (ClearHarbor Head of ML Ops), Andre Ramos (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (VP Product), Samir Kaur (Data Scientist)

Summary:
Monthly health check focusing on usage trends, unit economics, an incident follow-up from last month, and alignment on roadmap + benchmark plan. Customer requests a deeper run in a private staging VPC and wants clear next steps on cost optimization (caching/batching/quantization) and compliance docs.

Topics:
- Usage & spend trends (last 90 days)
- Recent latency incident and fallbacks
- Dedicated vs Hosted capacity planning
- Observability and audit log needs (SAML/KMS)
- Roadmap items: model rollouts, canary policies, and Optimize recommendations

Action items (recorded in call notes): see metadata for structured items.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hi everyone, thanks for joining, gonna kick off quick — appreciate you all making time, we have about 45 minutes, is that still good?
[00:18] Jasmine (ClearHarbor): yep that's fine, thanks Maya. we have Priya and Andre and Samir on as well, will keep this focused.
[00:30] Tom (Redwood CSM): quick agenda, usage, incident recap, then workshop on optimization and next steps.
[00:43] Priya (ClearHarbor): perfect, start with usage — we've seen a 2.5x spike month-on-month for our product recommendations, curious where that came from.
[01:05] Maya: yeah we pulled the run rate — looks like a lot of growth from your new A/B test and wider rollout last month. Andre, is that expected?
[01:20] Andre (ClearHarbor): yeah we moved to 24/7 traffic for the personalization pipeline, so steady traffic increased. we also changed prompt sets which increased token length.
[01:38] Luis (Redwood SE): that token length jump explains it — cost goes with tokens, and longer sequences hit KV cache patterns differently. we noticed your median seq jumped from 120 tokens to ~330.
[01:58] Samir (ClearHarbor): oh that high? hmm we thought most were short, maybe a few heavy requests skewing it.
[02:12] Maya: okay that'll inform batching suggestions — our Optimize engine flagged your workload as a candidate for prefix KV caching and a quantized model path.
[02:27] Jasmine: can you remind us what quantized model path means operationally? we've been cautious about quality regressions.
[02:42] Luis: sure — quantization reduces memory and inference cost by using lower precision kernels, in practice for many of the open models you keep within a small quality delta. we run eval prompts to check regressions. we can run your eval set as part of the benchmark.
[03:05] Priya: good, we'd need a clear pass/fail criteria; even a 1-2% drop in click-through is material.
[03:20] Tom: totally — we usually tie quality thresholds to your CI-eval and will gate rollouts via canary and A/B. we can wire alerts into the Console for regression.
[03:36] Andre: on the incident from Oct 25 — our SRE saw 503 spikes for a 20-minute window. can you walk through what happened?
[03:48] Maya: yes quick recap, there was a regional capacity constraint and our smart routing failed over to a compatible but heavier model variant which increased latency and pushed queue depth; fallbacks were triggered but some requests exceeded SLOs.
[04:10] Luis: to add, mixing burst traffic with large seq lengths caused a transient KV cache thrash on the serving layer; we pushed a fix for more aggressive pre-warming and adjusted autoscale policy.
[04:30] Jasmine: were logs sufficient for audit? our security team wanted detailed traces per token.
[04:42] Tom: audit logs are there but the format was slightly different than your SIEM ingestion — we'll export a sample bundle and Tom will follow up with the mapping.
[04:58] Maya: action item — we'll send the incident packet plus a timeline and remediation steps.
[05:06] Priya: thanks. on capacity, we were evaluating whether to move some pipelines to Dedicated capacity for predictability. thoughts?
[05:20] Luis: Dedicated helps with throughput and predictable p99 latency — cost is higher but you avoid noisy neighbors and capacity surprises. For mixed traffic a hybrid approach often works: host baseline on Hosted, move hot paths or very latency-sensitive routes to Dedicated.
[05:42] Andre: what's the break-even? our finance wants a number versus current spend.
[05:50] Maya: we can model that — we'll provide a 6/12-month forecast comparing continued Hosted plus Optimize changes vs reserved Dedicated commit. we'll include token-level unit economics.
[06:05] Samir: also curious about regional routing — we're expanding into EU and need data residency.
[06:15] Luis: we have region routing and can pin traffic to EU nodes; for strict residency we recommend Private (VPC) deployment where the control plane is private and data never leaves your VPC.
[06:34] Jasmine: Private is interesting but needs KMS/HSM integration and audit trail proof points.
[06:41] Tom: we have a compliance packet with KMS pattern examples, HSM addendum, and SOC2 attestations — I'll send that.
[06:51] Priya: what's the onboarding overhead for Private? timeline?
[06:58] Maya: typically 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and sizing; we have a playbook for network peering and a checklist for firewall rules.
[07:10] Andre: can Redwood run a staging deployment in our cloud for benchmarking before commit?
[07:18] Luis: yes we can spin a private staging env for benchmarking, ideally with your sample traffic or a replay. we'll need a VPC peering or secured dataset share.
[07:32] Samir: we can provide a 48-hour replay window and a curated eval set.
[07:41] Luis: perfect — we'll design the run: baseline (hosted) vs ded (dedicated) vs quantized variant; measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics.
[07:57] Jasmine: timeline?
[08:00] Maya: propose week of Nov 22 for a 2-3 day benchmark, if Andre can provision access.
[08:10] Andre: I'll aim to have staging open by Nov 15.
[08:18] Tom: recording next steps — Maya will send cost breakdown, Luis will send benchmarking plan, Andre will provide access.
[08:28] Priya: on observability, we want token-level tracing and trace context passing to our APM — how feasible?
[08:38] Luis: we support propagating trace headers and token-level metadata in audit logs, though token payloads are redacted by default. we can include correlation ids to stitch traces.
[08:51] Samir: fine with redaction as long as we can map request ids.
[08:56] Maya: noted. also Optimize identified a specific route where batching could give 3x throughput; it's a near-term win.
[09:08] Jasmine: does batching increase latency for single-request flows?
[09:14] Luis: batching is workload-aware — Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and can isolate low-latency paths; you can set per-route latency SLOs to avoid added latency for interactive routes.
[09:29] Priya: curious about model variants — we want to pin a version for 30 days and then roll to new weights, how are rollouts handled?
[09:40] Tom: Console supports canary percentages, auto-rollback on regression, and labeling of model versions. we can also schedule rollouts out of business hours.
[09:53] Jasmine: great. one more thing — procurement asked about support SLAs for P1 incidents.
[10:00] Maya: for Dedicated and Private we have SLA tiers; Hosted has an operational SLA but enterprise SLA is part of the reserved contract. we'll include SLA options in the follow-up.
[10:12] Andre: any notable competitor features we should watch? we heard some vendors offer pre-built embeddings cache.
[10:20] Maya: yes some competitors offer sticky cache layers but Redwood's approach is model-aware KV caching and cross-request prefix caching which tends to be more effective for long context workloads.
[10:35] Priya: ok let's wrap with explicit next steps.
[10:40] Maya: recap — Maya: send cost breakdown and incident packet by Friday; Luis: send benchmark plan and test vectors by Nov 12; Andre: provide staging access by Nov 15; Tom: send SOC2/KMS packet. schedule benchmark week of Nov 22.
[11:01] Jasmine: all good from our side. thanks all.
[11:08] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in calendar invites and email.

(End of recording)
